2027-04-23.title: Mar Geevarghese Sahada · St George the Great Martyr · Friday of the third week after Qyomtho
readings: Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus
Sheep in the midst of wolves; the one who endures to the end will be saved
2027-04-23.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Third Sunday after Qyomtho. The Panchangam keeps today the feast of Mar Geevarghese Sahada, St George the Martyr.
2027-04-23.verse: Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
theo: There is hardly a Christian village in Kerala without a Geevarghese, a Varghese or a George. The name of today's saint has passed from Syriac (Giwargis) into Malayalam homes, and his image, a young soldier on a white horse with his lance aimed at the dragon, hangs in churches of every tradition among us. Today our Church keeps his feast. What history can say with confidence is short and strong. George was a Christian soldier who gave his life for Christ in the great persecution of the early fourth century, most likely under the emperor Diocletian, and his tomb at Lydda (Diospolis) in Palestine was a place of pilgrimage within a few generations. The longer stories of his trials grew up later; the Church has always honoured him above all as a witness. Our tradition calls him Sahada, the Syriac word for martyr, which means witness. A decree attributed to Pope Gelasius I placed him among those whose names are rightly revered among people but whose deeds are known fully only to God (in substance). That is enough. We do not need every detail of his story to know what he did: when the empire demanded that he deny Christ, he chose Christ.

The readings show why a soldier became the image of every Christian. St Paul writes to Timothy: “You then, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus... Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus. No one serving in the army gets entangled in everyday affairs; the soldier's aim is to please the enlisting officer.” Paul adds the athlete, who is not crowned “without competing according to the rules,” and the farmer “who does the work.” All three are pictures of steady, faithful labour, not of sudden heroics. George's martyrdom did not come from nowhere; it grew out of a soldier's daily faithfulness to the one who had enlisted him in Baptism. St Ignatius of Antioch, himself on the way to martyrdom, wrote to Polycarp: please the one under whom you serve as soldiers; let none of you be found a deserter; let your Baptism be your shield, your faith your helmet, your love your spear, your endurance your armour (Letter to Polycarp 6, in substance). In the Gospel Jesus sends his disciples out with no illusions: “See, I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves; so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.” They will be handed over and “dragged before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and the Gentiles.” And he adds the promise that every martyr has leaned on: “do not worry about how you are to speak or what you are to say... for it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.” Finally: “the one who endures to the end will be saved.”

Why does a martyr's feast belong in the season of Qyomtho? Because martyrs are the strongest proof that Christians really believe in the Resurrection. No one dies for a story he suspects to be false. St Augustine taught that it is not the suffering but the cause that makes a martyr (Letter 89, in substance): George is honoured not because he was tortured, but because he would not betray the risen Lord. The famous dragon is a later legend, best read as a picture: the dragon is the old enemy, and every Christian who refuses evil for Christ's sake strikes at it. In our own time Christians are still dragged before councils, in many lands, for the name of Jesus. Pray for them today. And ask yourself where your own small martyrdom lies: in refusing a bribe at the office, in telling the truth at home when a lie would be easier, in keeping Sunday when the world pulls the other way. Take part in the Holy Qurbono for the feast if you can, and if you bear his name, thank God for it and ask for his courage.
conn: 2 Timothy 2:3–4 and the life of St George: the soldier who pleased the one who enlisted him, even at the cost of his life.
Matthew 10:16–22: Jesus foretold that his witnesses would be handed over to governors; the martyrs are the fulfilment of his word and of his promise that the Spirit would speak through them.
Hebrews 12:1, read yesterday, speaks of a cloud of witnesses; today the Church honours one of them by the Syriac title Sahada.
fathers: Please the one under whom you serve as soldiers; let none of you be found a deserter. Let your Baptism be your shield, your faith your helmet, your love your spear, your endurance your armour (Letter to Polycarp 6, in substance).
It is not the punishment that makes a true martyr, but the cause for which he suffers (Letter 89, in substance).
magis: Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith: the martyr bears witness to Christ who died and rose, to whom he is united by charity.
The Church has gathered with great care the records of those who persevered to the end in witnessing to their faith: these are the acts of the martyrs.
The Church considers martyrdom an exceptional gift and the highest proof of love, by which the disciple is made like the Master who willingly accepted death for the salvation of the world.
outline: Ask: what does it cost me today to be known as a Christian?

live: Pray today for Christians who are on trial, in prison or in danger for the name of Jesus.
Choose one place this week where you will refuse something wrong, quietly and firmly, for Christ's sake.
2027-04-23.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you gave Mar Geevarghese the courage of a good soldier and the crown of a martyr. You sent your disciples as sheep among wolves and promised that your Spirit would speak through them. By his prayers make us strong in your grace; let us not be entangled in what is passing, but seek only to please you who enlisted us in Baptism. Strengthen all Christians who suffer for your name, and give us endurance to the end, so that with all your witnesses we may share in your Resurrection. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The martyrs drew their strength from the altar: in the Holy Qurbono the Lord who laid down his life and rose again gives himself to us, the bread of those who bear witness.

quick: Mar Geevarghese Sahada (St George) was a Christian soldier martyred in the early fourth century; his tomb at Lydda drew pilgrims from early times.
Paul tells Timothy to share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus, who seeks to please the one who enlisted him.
Jesus sends his witnesses like sheep among wolves, promising that the Spirit of the Father will speak through them.
2027-04-23.action: Pray by name today for one country where Christians are persecuted.
2027-04-23.question: Where is my small daily martyrdom, the place where I must choose Christ against what is easy?
term: The Syriac word for martyr, meaning witness. Our Church gives this title to those who bore witness to Christ by shedding their blood, such as Mar Geevarghese Sahada.
kidsaint: St George was a brave soldier who loved Jesus more than his own life. Long after he died, people told a story about him killing a fierce dragon to save a princess and a whole town. The dragon is a picture of evil and sin. Lesson: whenever you say no to something wrong because you love Jesus, you are fighting the dragon like St George.

family.explain: Today is the feast of Mar Geevarghese, St George. He was a soldier, and when he was told to stop being a Christian, he said no, and he gave his life for Jesus. St Paul says every Christian is like a soldier of Jesus: we stay faithful every day, even when it is hard. Our weapons are prayer, truth and love.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in the world who are hurt or put in prison because they love Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for me to stand up for what is right? How can we help one another?”

illus: A young police constable from Kottayam, named Geevarghese after the saint like his grandfather, was posted to a checkpost on a busy highway. In his first month a lorry driver slid a folded note across with his papers. The older men at the post took such notes as a matter of course, and they laughed when he handed it back. For weeks they made his duty hard: the worst shifts, the longest nights. On the feast of his patron he went to the Qurbono before his shift and stood a little longer than usual before the saint's picture. That night he handed back two more notes. Years later one of those older colleagues, near retirement, told him that it was watching him refuse that had made him stop.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you made Mar Geevarghese a faithful soldier and a witness of your Resurrection. Make us strong in your grace. Amen.
share: Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 2:3). What suffering for Christ am I being asked to share?
I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves (Matthew 10:16). Where do I feel like a sheep among wolves?
The one who endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 10:22). What helps me to endure?
pm.resp: By the prayers of Mar Geevarghese, strengthen us, O Lord.
interc: For Christians persecuted for their faith today, that the Spirit may speak through them and keep them faithful.
For soldiers, police and all in uniform, that they may serve with justice and honesty.
For all who bear the name Geevarghese or George, that they may share the courage of their patron.
For those tempted to deny Christ for safety or gain.
For our parish and our Church, that we may be true witnesses of the risen Lord.
pm.close: Father, you crowned Mar Geevarghese with the glory of martyrdom. By his prayers make us good soldiers of Christ, wise and innocent among the wolves of this world, and keep us faithful to the end, so that we may rise with your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today our Church honours Mar Geevarghese Sahada, St George, a Christian soldier who gave his life for Christ in the great persecution of the early fourth century. Sahada means martyr, and martyr means witness. His tomb at Lydda drew pilgrims from very early times, and his name lives in countless Kerala families.

St Paul writes: share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus. No one serving in the army gets entangled in everyday affairs; the soldier's aim is to please the enlisting officer (2 Timothy 2:3–4). George served an earthly emperor, but his first loyalty was to Christ, who enlisted him in Baptism.

Jesus did not hide the cost: see, I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves (Matthew 10:16). His witnesses would be dragged before governors and kings. But he promised: it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you, and the one who endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 10:20, 22).

The martyrs belong to Qyomtho, because no one dies for a lie: they died for the risen Lord whom they knew. The dragon of the legend is evil itself. Each time we refuse evil for Christ, we strike it. Let us pray for persecuted Christians today, and ask Mar Geevarghese for the courage to be faithful soldiers in small things. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today is the feast of Mar Geevarghese, St George. Do you know anyone called Varghese or George? They are named after him! He was a soldier who loved Jesus so much that he would not stop being a Christian, even when the emperor ordered him. There is a famous story of him fighting a dragon. The dragon means everything bad. When you say no to lying or hitting or cheating because you love Jesus, you are as brave as St George!

intro: Theme: “Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.”
On the feast of Mar Geevarghese Sahada: the good soldier, the sheep among wolves, and the witness of the Resurrection.

points.h: A good soldier of Christ Jesus
sub: Pleasing the one who enlisted us.
q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his power. Put on the whole armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
points.apply: Each morning this week, before work or school, make the sign of the Cross slowly and offer the day to Christ as his soldier.

points.h: Sheep in the midst of wolves
sub: Wise as serpents, innocent as doves.
q: Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I fear no evil; for you are with me;
Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
points.apply: Pray by name for one country where Christians suffer for their faith, and learn one fact about their situation.

points.h: Sahada: a witness of the risen Lord
sub: No one dies for a lie.
The dragon and our daily refusals.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods
But they have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, for they did not cling to life even in the face of death.

concl: Mar Geevarghese was faithful in a soldier's daily duty, and so he was faithful in the hour of trial.
The martyrs are witnesses of Qyomtho: they died because they knew the Lord was alive.
2027-04-23.resolve: Be strong in grace, pray for persecuted Christians, and make one faithful refusal for Christ this week.
